description: Jake requests tiny gripper version TWO: "It should just be the same as the large grippers in every way, but just shrunk down." This explicitly corrects v1 Base 16/Gripper 23 v317_generalist_micro_tweezers, which redesigned the fingers as tweezers and replaced the large three-gear drive with direct two-gear drive. Create a NEW version and preserve v1. Source the large Base 15/Gripper 22 v316_generalist_post_cap explicitly (user-named large source overrides newest-part default): retain its actual curved/lattice finger outlines, loop pivots, separate handle-gears and pinion, tooth counts/ratios, captured posts/plain cap, proportions and kinematics. Prefer a uniform parametric scaling of the real source geometry, not another redesigned tweezer approximation. Carry forward original tiny target: no wider than STS3215 narrow dimension 24.8 mm, including full intended moving stroke. Publish as Tiny V2 with separate next Base and Gripper counters and unambiguous lineage. A real servo, horn and screws cannot be uniformly shrunk: do not scale hardware and claim it fits. Produce the faithful miniature CAD concept and clearly separate any minimum necessary full-size hardware adapter/interface from the scaled mechanism; if strict exact scaling plus hardware fit is infeasible, document exact measured interference and label concept/not build-ready rather than silently redesigning the requested shape. Scale factor and all dimensions in params.json, preview Tune support and correct pivots; maintain existing versions. Render side-by-side large versus tiny to show fidelity. Export parts, run manifold/volume and complete-motion collision/continuous-width checks, and add regressions that reject altered proportions/gear ratio, excessive stroke or width. Verify preview catalog and compatible picks. Use GPT-6.1 Sol medium; own the single reply, explicit-path commit and give-to-human. CAD exports are required; no application build. Shared checkout: unrelated Generated/GitInfo.swift is not yours. Voice session is doing no CAD edits, so there is no competing implementation this time.

results.identified_issue:
Followed latest human authorization: width cap and original gear counts/ratio/uniform whole-mechanism scaling were revoked. Do not revert to the 17% non-mountable concept or the obsolete 90% fixed-gear result. Base 17 explicitly derives from Base 15, and Gripper 24 from Gripper 22, preserving Tiny V1 and large source. Recognizable original curved lattice fingers/taper are uniformly 50% except actual-size loop clearance. Drive is 30:30:24, module 1.045, ratio 1.25:1 instead of 2.125:1; servo stroke 37.5 degrees for full 30 degree jaws. Real STS3215 is sideways (180 degree body), which avoids cutting away right pivot support with the label-hump window. Four-M2 rail and four-M3 horn mount stay actual size; stock horn phase corrected to 45 degrees. Base/cap/pillars and countersink recess adapted locally; arm wrist tab/pilots omitted for standalone use. Full physical hardware dimensions and working clearances are compensated in params.py before output scaling.
Bounded analytical search compares scale 20–100% by 1%, all integer tooth counts 18–40. Adopted allowances: lattice ligament >=0.4 mm for fine resin, module >=1, countersink rim >=1. Selected 50%, 30:24 minimizes scale then estimated width then pinion pitch radius within that search. 49% with resized gears fits hardware but lattice is 0.39663 mm; 40% can fit hardware with other counts but lattice is 0.32378 mm. Selected lattice 0.404726 and screw rim 1.03375 mm: very thin margins, not ordinary FDM or strength-certified. No global optimum claim. Smaller reinforced fingers, modified lattice, different manufacturing or horns remain outside this bounded comparison.
Selected exports: 14 individual mechanism meshes watertight, consistently wound, positive volume, one component. Genus matches retained holes; base drops two unused wrist pilots. Original finger modules/trace and outer vertices checked. 7,986 full-range sampled pair checks at 0.25 degree intervals include servo, cable keep-out, and screw probes, all pass. Width/height use analytic continuous vertex extrema, not sampled bounds. Positive controls verify tooth phase interference and servo/pinion seating. Screw probes omit intended threaded engagement. Candidate screws M3x12 horn (2.5 mm engagement, 1.2 mm tip/case clearance), M2x6 case (4 mm assumed engagement), M3x10 cap (7 mm bite, 0.3 mm pilot-bottom clearance). Case thread depth is inherited 4 mm assumption and must be measured. No print, physical fit, torque, wear or strength tests performed.
Six Tiny V2 regressions, 13 gallery tests, 15 publisher tests, SCAD hinge consistency and JS syntax check pass. The broad pre-existing every-gripper pose suite also exposed an unrelated missing v306 hinge entry; left that item untouched. CAD-only publisher ran with --no-build. Catalog/mix pickers show independent Base 17 and Gripper 24 lineage and flag incompatible fingers. New uniform_scale motion support preserves pinion Z pivot through Tune. Generated/GitInfo.swift was unrelated and never committed.
results.summary: Tiny V2 now has half-size original fingers, resized gears and the real STS3215 mounting.
results.detailed_description:
Base 17 + Gripper 24 keeps the curved lattice fingers at 50% size, with a new 30:30:24 drive and direct stock servo/horn mounting. The full moving envelope is 70.03 mm wide × 114.51 mm high × 62.90 mm deep, including cable clearance.

The selected CAD passes mesh, stroke, mounting and preview checks. Its retained lattice reaches 0.405 mm walls, so this is a fine-resin prototype with no load rating. Review the attached comparison and CAD; confirm thread depths, print and test fit next.

results.notes: LATEST DESIGN AUTHORIZATION from Jake: "We can change any of the gear sizes, that is fine. The only limit is really ... the servo mounting screws probably." Keep actual servo mounting screw pattern, horn and screw dimensions correct; account for real clearances and material thickness rather than claiming screw spacing is the sole physical constraint.
